title: Guardians add Foster Griffin, trading 4 minor leaguers to Nats to boost rotation
author: Spencer Nusbaum
content:
The Cleveland Guardians on Monday added an All-Star to one of the league’s best rotations, acquiring left-hander Foster Griffin from the Washington Nationals for a package of four prospects within 30 minutes of the league’s trade deadline.

In return for one of this year’s upstart players, the Nationals received pitchers Will Dion, Josh Hartle and Kendeglys Virguez and outfielder Nick Mitchell to Washington.

Griffin was one of three All-Stars on the upstart Nationals, posting a 2.77 ERA across 110 1/3 innings heading into the first half. Though he’s probably not your idea of a modern starter — his fastball sits 91-92 mph — he strikes out more batters than you think and has been uber-effective this season thanks to exceptional command, even better game-planning and a seven-pitch mix.

He joins a Guardians rotation that already had the sixth-best ERA in the league. The addition will likely shift Slade Cecconi to another role, perhaps in the bullpen. The Guardians already skipped his turn in the rotation on Sunday. But with Parker Messick and Gavin Williams pitching like front-line starters and Tanner Bibee having rebounded from a sluggish start to the season, adding an All-Star to the rotation is one way to compensate for what’s been one of the league’s worst offenses.

In his first year back stateside after three seasons in Japan, Griffin, a 30-year-old rookie, has a 3.06 ERA, a 1.08 WHIP and 116 strikeouts over 129 1/3 innings.

He probably won’t start Game 1 in October, but there is more than enough in the tank to suggest he can start a postseason game. If there is one flaw to note, it is his propensity for giving up home runs. Teams have hit 19 against him, with the two he’s allowed in the second half hit by the Atlanta Braves on Friday.

But the top-line metrics are encouraging. Griffin’s ability to navigate a lineup and dominate left-handed hitters is an attractive feature that has held up against some of MLB’s top lineups this year. And he’s been as consistent as they come: Griffin didn’t allow more than one earned run in eight starts from June 5 to July 19.

Griffin is a rental, which is why the Guardians didn’t part with any prospects ranked within miles of the top of their organizational rankings. They acquired Hartle and Mitchell as part of the three-team swap last December that sent shortstop Andrés Giménez to the Toronto Blue Jays and landed pitcher Luis Ortiz in Cleveland. Dion has made 12 appearances for the Guardians this season and has logged a 4.58 ERA.
